clue.text: Head of cult, arrogant, snoops on them at first

parts.note: high, as in high and mighty, means arrogant
pries means snoops or noses about

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word them

parts.note: first letter of them

explanation.surface: A cult leader is arrogant and spies on followers from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief priest presides over a religion or sect, so he is the leading figure of a cult.

clue.text: Awful cheek pinching line, so barrack

indicators.note: pinching means holding tightly, so the jumbled word grips the line letter
awful suggests something messed up, so the letters of cheek are jumbled

explanation.surface: Terrible insolence, nicking a line, so jeer.
explanation.walkthrough: To barrack is the British sense of jeering at a speaker or performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrack is a verb meaning to jeer or shout down a speaker, the same as interrupting with taunts.

clue.text: Bishop leaving rubbish in lock-up?

indicators.note: leaving says the bishop letter departs from the word

parts.note: garbage is rubbish
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A cleric leaves junk stashed in a storage unit.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a lock-up is a rented garage or storage unit that can be secured; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock-up garage is a separate securable building for keeping a car, often rented apart from the home.

clue.text: Declarations made by you and me, say, about building material

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the pronouns go round the building material

parts.note: you and me are examples of pronouns
cement is a building material

explanation.surface: Statements made by the two of us concerning construction supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronouncements are formal statements or announcements, so they are declarations.

clue.text: Office-holder lying

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person who currently holds a post

explanation.walkthrough: Lying looks like it means telling untruths, a dig at politicians, but here it means reclining.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it names the current holder of an office; as an adjective it means reclining or resting on something.

clue.text: After that time, close to Christmas, in church

indicators.note: close to means the end, so take the final letter of Christmas

parts.note: last letter of Christmas
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: At a festive season, the period approaching Christmas spent in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Since as an adverb means from that point onwards, from a time in the past till now.

clue.text: Record time taken by primate

indicators.note: taken by places the time letter alongside, ahead of, the primate

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A recording of a time trial captured by a monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: To record something on magnetic media is to tape it; the verb senses match.

clue.text: Word puzzle bringing on a vexed moment, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the phrase is heard, not spelt

parts.note: the indefinite article, A; cross means vexed or annoyed; a tick is a moment, as in 'just a tick'

explanation.surface: A crossword-type puzzle that brings on irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross is vexed and a tick is a brief moment in British usage, so a cross tick is a vexed moment.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrostic is a puzzle or verse in which the initial letters of lines spell out a word.

clue.text: Service still good around end of session

indicators.note: around means the first words wrap round the next letter

parts.note: even so means still or nevertheless

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of session

parts.note: last letter of session

explanation.surface: A worship service that is still good once a session ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts EVENSOG round the N from the end of session.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening prayer service in the Anglican church.

clue.text: Sloth or pride?

parts.note: a sloth is a group of bears and a pride a group of lions, terms for a group of animals

explanation.walkthrough: Sloth and pride look like two of the deadly sins, but they are the names for groups of bears and of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammarians use this term for a word naming a group, such as flock, herd or pride.

clue.text: Piece of bric-à-brac inquisitive American dropped off

indicators.note: dropped off says the American letters fall away from the end of the word

parts.note: curious means inquisitive

explanation.surface: A nosy American tourist leaves an ornament behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A curio is a small unusual collectable object, the kind of knick-knack found among bric-à-brac.

clue.text: Conservative following the correct route for large hall

parts.note: on course means following the correct route

explanation.surface: A Tory finds the right way through to a big hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a large open space or hall in a station or airport where crowds gather.

clue.text: The French chap at wedding makes space

parts.note: le is French for the
the groom is the man getting married

explanation.surface: A French bridegroom clears some room for himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Legroom is the room available for one's legs, a particular kind of space in a seat or vehicle.

clue.text: Recruits unusually silent before start of service

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of silent are put in an unusual order
start of takes only the opening letter of service

parts.note: first letter of service

explanation.surface: New army recruits are strangely quiet before their first spell of duty.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist someone is to sign them up for service, which is what a recruiter does.

clue.text: Crossing in secret on it at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clandestine crossing being made by boat.
explanation.definitionFit: An intersection is a junction where roads or lines cross one another.

clue.text: Steps aboard vessel, craft on a long journey perhaps

definitions.text: craft on a long journey perhaps

indicators.note: aboard means on a ship, so the steps go inside the vessel

parts.note: a ship is a vessel
paces are steps

explanation.surface: Someone pacing the deck of a ship on a long voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaceship is a craft for travelling through space, often on very long trips; perhaps marks this as an example.

clue.text: Salad we locals prepared

indicators.note: prepared, as food is made ready, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A side dish made by the people from the area.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleslaw is a salad of shredded raw cabbage dressed with mayonnaise.

clue.text: European newspaper cuttings editor's hidden

parts.note: clips are pieces cut from newspapers
ED is the abbreviation for editor, with the 's meaning is

explanation.surface: A European editor has hidden away press cuttings.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eclipsed is obscured or covered, as the sun is during an eclipse.

clue.text: Where players play in front of play's players, perhaps

definitions.text: Where players play in front of play's players, perhaps

parts.words: Where players play in front of play's players, perhaps
parts.note: the first players are musicians, the second are actors on stage; the musicians sit in a sunken area in front of the stage

explanation.walkthrough: Players means two things here: musicians who play instruments, and actors performing a play.
explanation.definitionFit: This sunken area before the stage of a theatre houses the musicians accompanying a show.

clue.text: Cash in on find

parts.note: re means on or concerning
to deem is to judge or find, as a court finds

explanation.surface: Profiting from a discovery.
explanation.definitionFit: To redeem a voucher or bond is to exchange it for money, which is cashing it in.

clue.text: Stall bearing right for London thoroughfare

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the stall holds the right letter

parts.note: a stand is a market stall

explanation.surface: A market booth turning right onto a busy London street.
explanation.definitionFit: The Strand is a major street in central London running from Trafalgar Square to Fleet Street.

clue.text: Marked papers during meeting

indicators.note: during places the papers within the meeting

parts.note: an event, such as a race meeting
ID, identity papers

explanation.surface: Documents were graded in the course of a conference.
explanation.definitionFit: A marked difference is a clear, obvious one, so marked here is an adjective meaning plain to see.

clue.text: Organised tour encompassing river in county town

indicators.note: encompassing means surrounding, so the rearranged tour holds the river letter
organised means arranged, so the letters of tour are rearranged

explanation.surface: A guided trip taking in a river in a provincial town.
explanation.definitionFit: Truro is the county town of Cornwall in south-west England, its administrative centre and a cathedral city.

clue.text: Mountain, most demanding without foremost of Sherpas

indicators.note: without says the following letter is removed

parts.note: severest means hardest or most demanding

indicators.note: foremost of picks only the first letter of Sherpas

parts.note: first letter of Sherpas

explanation.surface: The toughest peak, tackled with no lead Sherpa guide.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's highest peak in the Himalayas, whose climbers famously rely on Sherpa guides.

clue.text: Failed to maintain contact, missing last letter in post — that hurt

parts.note: lost means missing

indicators.note: last letter in takes the final letter of post

parts.note: last letter of post
ouch is what someone says when hurt

explanation.surface: A letter has gone missing in the mail, which is painful for a correspondent.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose touch with someone is to stop being in communication, the idiom for failing to keep contact.

clue.text: Letter from Greece, and some from e.g. Argentina

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A letter arriving from Greece, and others from countries like Argentina.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Wife and I and daughter initially earned extra

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of earned

parts.note: first letter of earned

explanation.surface: A couple and their daughter at first earned some additional income.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach, and the run it gives counts as an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide is one of the cricket extras, runs added to the score not hit by a batter.

clue.text: Still furious? Obviously not!

parts.note: someone in a jumping rage is not still, since they are leaping about

explanation.walkthrough: Still seems to mean 'yet', but it is read as 'motionless'; a person in this kind of rage is physically bouncing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone extremely angry, as if jumping up and down with rage.
